Hans Krebs is known for describing the citric acid cycle.

During prophase I, chromosomes condense and spindle formation begins, but kinetochore fibres do not shorten to separate homologues.
During metaphase I, homologous chromosome pairs align at the cell equator.
During anaphase I, spindle fibres shorten and pull homologous chromosomes toward opposite poles.
During telophase I, chromosomes have reached the poles and the cell begins to divide.
